messages:
jen: AcmeCorp (acct: acme-01) — customer reports their daily CSV exports are blank for 2024-03-03 -> 2024-03-05. Dashboard and invoice show usage, but raw export files are 0 bytes. They attached the S3 paths they downloaded: s3://redwood-acme-exports/acme-01/2024-03-03.csv (0 bytes) , s3://redwood-acme-exports/acme-01/2024-03-04.csv (0 bytes)
lee: thx. Do we know which pipeline produced those CSVs? export manifest or job id?
jen: manifest shows generated_by: usage-agg-v2, shard: acme-01, manifest line: `2024-03-03, s3://redwood-acme-exports/acme-01/2024-03-03.csv, size:0, generated_by:usage-agg-v2, run_ts:2024-03-03T00:05:12Z`
ops-bot: usage-agg-v2 job run at 2024-03-03T00:05:12Z completed with exit code 0 (job-id: run-20240303-aggv2-acme-01)
sophie: curious — exit code 0 but zero rows. digging into aggregator logs for that run now. quick check: raw_events table shows tokens for acct acme-01 on those dates. So ingestion happened.
lee: can you paste the SQL you ran?
sophie: ran: ```sql
SELECT date(event_time) as day, count(*) as events, sum(token_count) as tokens
FROM raw_events
WHERE account_id = 'acme-01' AND date(event_time) between '2024-03-03' and '2024-03-05'
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day;
```
sophie: result: 2024-03-03 -> events: 2,345 tokens: 1,238,432 ; 2024-03-04 -> events: 1,987 tokens: 987,021 ; 2024-03-05 -> events: 2,102 tokens: 1,105,210
lee: so ingestion ok. exporter produced zero-row CSVs. I suspect the exporter filter step dropped rows due to a schema change in payload (token_count moved inside `usage.metrics` for a short migration window).
sophie: found this in aggregator log around the run:
```
2024-03-03T00:05:12Z INFO starting export for shard acme-01
2024-03-03T00:05:14Z WARN record missing expected field token_count, attempting fallback
2024-03-03T00:05:15Z ERROR exporter: all_records_filtered_out after applying schema filter
2024-03-03T00:05:15Z INFO completed export (rows:0) files_written:1
```
aiden: hmm there was a schema rollout on 2024-03-02 that put token_count under `usage.metrics.token_count` for new writes. Backwards compatibility code should have handled it but looks like the exporter had an expr that only read `payload.token_count` and didn't run the fallback map for a subset of shards.
lee: that matches. which commits touched exporter logic? @deploy-bot any deploys around 2024-03-02 -> 2024-03-03?
deploy-bot: deploy record: service=usage-exporter, version=3.9.7, deployed_at=2024-03-02T23:58:02Z, deploy_id=dep-20240302-usageexp-3.9.7
lee: bingo. 3.9.7 had a stricter schema filter. ops: we need a safe backfill for acme-01 for 2024-03-03..2024-03-05. plan: 1) run exporter in dry-run for those dates to confirm non-zero rows 2) run full export to S3 in a backfill path like s3://backfill/redwood-acme-exports/acme-01/2024-03-03.csv 3) update manifest and notify customer 4) add fix/rollback to exporter to re-enable fallback parsing. Agree?
jen: customer wants ETA. can we give an estimate?
lee: dry-run should be minutes. full backfill for 3 days for single shard < 30m. I'll do dry-run now and post results.
lee: running: `infra/run_export.sh --shard acme-01 --start 2024-03-03 --end 2024-03-05 --dry-run` — will paste output.
lee: dry-run output:
```
2024-03-07T18:10:01Z INFO dry-run export for acme-01 2024-03-03..2024-03-05
2024-03-07T18:10:05Z INFO day=2024-03-03 candidate_rows=2345 candidate_tokens=1238432
2024-03-07T18:10:07Z INFO day=2024-03-04 candidate_rows=1987 candidate_tokens=987021
2024-03-07T18:10:08Z INFO day=2024-03-05 candidate_rows=2102 candidate_tokens=1105210
2024-03-07T18:10:09Z INFO dry-run complete
```
lee: confirmed. Now scheduling actual backfill write to s3 backfill path. I'll include a safety flag to avoid overwriting primary path: `--output-prefix s3://backfill/redwood-acme-exports/ --no-overwrite-primary`
lee: kicked off backfill job at 2024-03-07T18:30Z, job-id backfill-19050-acme-01-01. will monitor.
ops-bot: backfill-19050-acme-01-01 status: RUNNING
sophie: quick note: before we hand this to customer, we should patch exporter to 1) read both `payload.token_count` and `usage.metrics.token_count` 2) add a short unit test covering both shapes. I'll open a tiny PR and request a rollback if needed.
lee: backfill finished at 2024-03-07T18:54Z. job-id backfill-19050-acme-01-01 result: SUCCESS. uploaded:
 - s3://backfill/redwood-acme-exports/acme-01/2024-03-03.csv (size: 1.2MB)
 - s3://backfill/redwood-acme-exports/acme-01/2024-03-04.csv (size: 970KB)
 - s3://backfill/redwood-acme-exports/acme-01/2024-03-05.csv (size: 1.1MB)
je n: shared backfill links to customer and asked them to re-download. customer confirms they can download and token counts match dashboard numbers.
jen: customer notes one file timestamp differs (2024-03-03 file shows generated_at 2024-03-07) — we told them that's expected for backfill and that invoices are unaffected. they asked for explanation for why primary files were zero; I sent brief note about a rolling schema change + exporter filter and that we've patched and will roll the fix shortly.
sophie: PR opened: github.com/redwood/usage-exporter/pull/412 — adds fallback and unit test. planning hotfix release 3.9.8 with fix and rollback guard.
aiden: scheduled hotfix deploy to prod at 2024-03-08T02:00Z (low traffic). will monitor.
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy dep-20240308-usageexp-3.9.8 at 2024-03-08T02:00:00Z
jen: marking support ticket SK-2291 as pending-customer-confirmation then resolved once they confirm success. customer is happy with backfill and patch plan.
lee: follow-up actions: 1) add export smoke check that compares csv row counts vs raw_events counts for every shard nightly 2) run a retrospective on schema rollout process to prevent exporter breakage
jen: thanks all :thumbsup!
